USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Do not stack new tariff hikes or fresh non-tariff measures on top of the August 1 List 4 announcement and the August 5 currency-manipulator designation. Keep List 3 at 25% and Huawei on the Entity List, but treat the September 1 List 4 effective date as a bargaining deadline rather than an irreversible lock-in. Reopen the already-scheduled early-September Washington round and condition any delay or consumer-goods carve-outs on China restoring agricultural purchases and putting enforceable IP/tech-transfer text back on the table. Unilateral rollback would reward the yuan break and the farm embargo; another escalation into holidays would tax U.S. consumers and deepen the market-priced recession risk.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is moderately elevated, not existential. The Osaka ceasefire (no new tariffs "for the time being") is already broken: after a thin Shanghai round, the U.S. announced 10% on the remaining ~$300B effective September 1, and China answered by letting CNY through 7 and suspending U.S. farm purchases. That hits a sector already cut from $19.5B (2017) to $9.1B (2018) in China-bound farm exports, which the Farm Bureau called a "body blow." List 4 is the first tranche that lands on phones, apparel, toys and other holiday consumer goods, so the Chamber of Commerce is right that U.S. households and retailers would pay. Markets are already treating this as a growth shock: the 10-year yield fell to 1.71% on August 7 (down ~94 bp in the window), the 3m–10y curve inverted to its most negative since 2007, and the Dow dropped 767 points (2.9%) on August 5. The Fed’s July 31 cut explicitly cited trade-policy uncertainty as a downside risk. That is material GDP/political drag and a key export sector under fire — above neutral, short of the +0.5 "high" anchor because the expansion is still intact, List 4 is not yet in force, and September talks remain on the calendar. Action stays near zero because further escalation would raise the chance China stays on a protracted-war footing and would feed the very consumer-price and farm-belt costs that are now the main threat to U.S. interests; concession without a matching Chinese offer would surrender remaining leverage after Beijing just retaliated. Negotiate, do not concede and do not pile on.
key_factors: Osaka ceasefire broken by List 4 announcement after a no-progress Shanghai round
China farm-purchase halt hits an already-damaged U.S. export sector
List 4 would be the first broad consumer-goods tariff wave before the holiday season
Market/Fed signal: 10-year at 1.71%, yield-curve inversion, July insurance cut, Aug 5 equity crash
Currency-manipulator label is mostly symbolic (IMF track) but opened a financial channel
September Washington talks still scheduled — a usable off-ramp without unilateral rollback

sources_cited.excerpt: After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
G20 Osaka: Trump and Xi agree to resume talks. Existing tariffs remain; no new tariffs "for the time being."
Trade talks in Shanghai (through July 31). Little progress reported.
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List.
10-year Treasury yield latest 1.71% on 2019-08-07; change -0.94 (-35%) over the window.
Federal funds effective rate 2.13% on 2019-08-01 after the late-July cut (from 2.40% in July).
New 10% duties hit cellphones, computers, shoes and apparel; Chamber: tariffs inflict greater pain on U.S. businesses, farmers, workers and consumers.
China Commerce Ministry: companies stopped buying U.S. farm products; Farm Bureau called it a body blow; China farm imports $9.1B in 2018 vs $19.5B in 2017.
Dow shed 767 points (worst day of 2019); 10-year yield ~1.72%; yield-curve inversion widest since April 2007.
Powell: July cut intended to insure against downside risks from weak global growth and trade policy uncertainty.
Treasury: China designated a currency manipulator; next step is IMF engagement, not automatic tariffs.
